cases.name: Christine Beye Dzienisiewski
cases.about:
Dzienisiewski taught for 12 years at Elizabeth's William F. Halloran School No. 22. District officials and her fellow teachers made arrangements to have their classes covered Monday morning so that several could attend the service. She taught sixth grade, but she had a personality and energy recognized throughout the whole building, said school Principal Michael Webb.

"Everybody knew her," he said. "She was just kind of the person that skipped down the halls. It's tough."

Some of Dzienisiewski's former students came to the funeral as well, saying after the service that she remained a favorite teacher, even years later. They recalled her as caring, with a constant smile.

Woodley Bouzy, now a junior, said Dzienisiewski was the first person to support him when he decided at one point he wanted to be a doctor, telling him not to let anyone keep him from his dream.

"She was one of the most interesting teachers," said Bouzy, 17. "She wasn't dull. She always made sure everybody was having fun."

"She knew how to keep everybody smiling," added Alyamise Hankins, 17, another former student.
